full_judgment:
2. The Facts of the case, in brief, are that on 19.4.2003 at about 5.30 p.m. deceased Sreekanta Rakshit, younger son of informant Shikha Rakshit and Advocate Mridul Kanti Rakshit, with his friend Jashim Uddin Jessy went out of their house at 44 Hazari Lane under Kotwali Police Station of Chittagong City. But he did not return home. The informant contacted Jashim Uddin alias Jessy over telephone and came to know that Sreekanta had got down from his rickshaw in front of Collegiate School on Ice Factory Road. The informant became anxious as Sreekanta was not returning home. At midnight she informed the matter to Kotwali Police Station. Early in the morning she informed her elder son Sree Kumar Rakshit in Dhaka over telephone. Her husband, Mridul Kanti Rakshit and her daughter used to live in Dhaka in the house of his elder son Sree Kumar Rakshit. She asked her elder son, husband and daughter to rush to Chittagong. At about 12.30 p.m. she received a telephone call, in which someone naming himself as Bhola informed her that the beheaded dead body of her son Sreekanta was lying in Hathazari Police Station. She contacted Hathazari Police Station over telephone and came to know that the beheaded dead body recovered from Lala Chandra Beel of village Shikarpur had already been sent to the morgue for post mortem examination. At 2.30 p.m. her elder son arrived home from Dhaka and went to the morgue with his maternal uncle Shovan. They identified the beheaded dead body as that of the deceased. Further, the prosecution case was that accused Azimuddin Mahmud alias Azam, Abdul Hamid, Man Chowdhury, Jahangir Alam, Paritosh Rakshit, Kazal Rakshit, Aparup Rakshit, Arun Rakshit, Baron Rakshit and others had dispute with the father of the deceased over his dwelling house at 44 Hazari Lane. On 25.12.1998 they forcibly occupied a room of the building. Since then accused Elahijan, mother of accused Azimuddin, with her domestic help and maid used to live there. The informant filed a criminal case against those accused persons at Kotwali Police Station. Police guards were posted in the house for the safety and security of the members of the informant's family. Accused A.B.M. Fazle Karim Chowdhury, a Member of the Parliament, also had enmity with the father of the deceased. He, with a view to grab the property of the father of the deceased, put pressure on him in different ways so that he left the country. On 27.3.2003 at 8.00 p.m. accused Jahangir Alam, Irfan Chowdhury, Paritosh Rakshit, Kazal Rakshit, Arun Rakshit, Saroj Guha, Abdul Hamid, Baron Rakshit, Amit Rakshit and others assembled in the room of accused Elahijan and hatched a conspiracy to kill the deceased in order to occupy the remaining portion of the house. On 16.04.2003 at 12.30 noon, in the office of accused A.B.M. Fazle Karim Chowdhury at Agrabad Commercial Area, the accused persons made conspiracy to kill the deceased. Accordingly, on the night following 19.4.2003, the accused persons taking the deceased to the vacant flat in the ground floor of Building No.1 of Safi Haji at Purba Madarbari, slaughtered him and dumped his beheaded dead body in Lala Chandra Beel and the severed head in Mahamaya Canal. 

 3. Next day, on 20.4.2003 at 9.55 p.m., the informant lodged FIR with Double Mooring Police Station, naming Azimuddin Mahmud, Abdul Hamid, Paritosh Rakshit, Irfan Chowdhury, Jahangir Alam, Kazal Rakshit, Aparup Rakshit, Arun Rakshit, Barun Rakshit, Amit Rakshit and Saroj Guha as accused. During investigation of the case accused Dipak Datta Bhola was arrested. His confession led to recovery of the severed head of the deceased. Then accused Dipak Datta Bhola, Jahangir Alas and Md. Mobarak Hossain made confessional statements recorded by the Magistrates under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Police after investigation of the case submitted charge-sheet against seventeen accused persons of whom Azimuddin Mahmud, Elahijan and Paritosh Rakshit were absconding. The accused persons were; put on trial in the Druto Bichar Tribunal, Chittagong, wherein charge under sections 120B/302/201/34 of the Penal Code was framed against them, to which the accused persons on dock pleaded innocence and demanded justice Absconding accused Azimuddin Mahmud, Elahijan and Paritosh Rakshit were defended by a State Defence lawyer in the trial held in their absence. 

 4. The defence case, as it appears from the trend of cross-examination of the prosecution witnesses and statements made by some accused persons while examined under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, is that of innocence and false implication. The confessional statements of accused Dipak Dutta Bhola, Jahangir Alam and Mobarak Hossain were not voluntary and true. Those were extracted by inducement, threat, coercion, torture and intimidation. 

 6. The learned Judge of the Tribunal on consideration of the evidence on record and the facts and circumstances of the case convicted and sentenced twelve accused persons and acquitted the remaining five. He found that the prosecution failed to prove the charge of criminal conspiracy allegedly committed on 16.04.2003 in the office of accused A.B.M. Fazle Karim Chowdhury at, Agrabad Commercial Area. He however convicted seven accused persons, namely Paritosh Rakshit (absconding), Abdul Hamid, Irfan Chowdhury, Arun Rakshit, Barun Rakshit, Saroj Guha and Kazal Rakshit under section 120B of the Penal Code for hatching criminal conspiracy of killing the deceased on 27.03.2003 at 8.00 p.m. in the room of accused Elahijan in the building of holding No.44 Hazari Lane. But accused Azimuddin Mahmud, Kamrul Hasan Titu, Jahangir and Dipak Datta Bhola were not convicted for such criminal conspiracy. 

 7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order of conviction and sentence, convict Kazal Rakshit preferred Criminal Appeal No. 2006 of 2004, convicts Arun Rakshit, Barun Rakshit, Saroj Guha, Irfan Chowdhury and Abdul Hamid jointly preferred Criminal Appeal No. 2208 of 2004 and convicts Dipak Datta Bhola, Jahangir Alam, Mobarak Hossain and Kamrul Hasan Titu respectively preferred Jail Appeal Nos. 578, 579, 580 and 581 of 2004. Convicts Azimuddin Mahmud and Paritosh Rakshit have been absconding as before. The State filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.5069 of 2004 under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure against the order of acquittal of five accused persons, and the informant filed Criminal Revision No.856 of 2004 under sections 439/435 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for enhancement of sentence of seven accused persons convicted under section 120B of the Penal Code. The wife of the condemned prisoner also filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.14993 of 2005 under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure challenging the order dated 21.11.2004 passed by the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Chittagong in Criminal Revision No. 284 of 2004 affirming the order dated 5.7.2004 passed by the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong in C.R. Case No. 200 of 2003 staying further proceedings of the case till disposal of the Death Reference. The High Court Division found the rule issued in this miscellaneous case to be infructuous. The Rules issued in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.5069 of 2004 and Criminal Revision No.856 of 2004 were discharged. 

 9. Mr. Md. Helaluddin Mollah, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the case against the petitioner was false and concocted by the police for failure to pay a large sum of money as demanded by the police officer and for refusing to compromise the case concerning the murder of his own brother. He submits that the case was not proved beyond reasonable doubt by legal evidence. He submits that the petitioner was not named in the FIR and was not identified by the informant in the dock. He further submits that the conviction of the petitioner was based on his confessional statement which was extorted by police torture and is clearly exculpatory, and, therefore, the High Court Division erred in accepting the Death Reference. He further submits that Article 103 of the Constitution has been; amended by Act No.14 of 2011 whereby it is now provided that if the High Court Division upholds the sentence of death or imposes the sentence of death or life imprisonment upon any accused then the accused shall be entitled to prefer appeal as of right before the Appellate Division. He finally submits that since the Constitution has been amended giving a beneficial right to the accused, the same right shall accrue to the petitioner although his appeal before the High Court Division was disposed of by a judgment and order which was passed; before the amendment to the Constitution.
